title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Theophrastus iris perfume separates liquid loss from quality under pre-treatment
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The source links prior steeping with reduced oil absorption, but singles out dry unheated iris-root for superior perfume; it also recommends removing spices before excess absorption. Pre-treatment affects uptake and liquid loss; a separately scoped iris quality comparison can favor the dry unheated route. Contact duration changes absorption without changing spice identity. Quantity recovered and quality obtained are different outcomes, not one generic beneficial state.

design.contrast: A monotonic improvement account makes reduced waste imply better perfume. An ingredient-list account drops pre-treatment and removal time. A universal dry-is-better account overextends the specifically iris-qualified quality claim.
design.prediction: A coherent account must allow lower loss to coexist with a different preferred quality route, and bind the removed spices to the same batch that absorbed oil. Preserve the source tension between more complete virtue in dry iris and the separately stated squeezing-out effect of prior steeping; do not repair it into modern chemistry.
